subject: Ownership boundaries & dataflow mapping for DPA — Medisoft follow-up
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@medisoft.io>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medisoft Legal <legal@medisoft.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on ownership & transfers in DPA — Medisoft

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal has flagged two items in the draft DPA and appendix related to LLM data handling where we need more precision before we can sign:

1) Ownership and downstream rights: the DPA currently references "outputs" and "derivative models". We need explicit language that: (a) customer prompts and model responses are owned by Medisoft, and (b) Redwood will not use Medisoft data to improve models (no-training) unless we opt in via a separate agreement and controls.

2) Cross-border processing: Medisoft is an EU controller; we require a clear map of subprocessors, locations where tokens or KV cache might be persisted, and whether any model snapshots or aggregated telemetry could be transferred outside the EEA.

Can you provide: a) a simple dataflow diagram we can attach to the DPA; b) a timestamped inventory of subprocessors w/ countries; and c) a short confirmation for our security team about "no-training" options and exportability of customer exports.

We'd like these by end of week if possible — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Elena
Head of Integrations, Medisoft

[Attachment: medisoft-dpa-markup.pdf (referenced)]

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@medisoft.io>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on ownership & transfers in DPA — Medisoft

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I looped in Naomi (privacy) and David (infrastructure) so we can answer all parts. High level answers up front:

• Ownership: we can confirm that by default customers retain ownership of prompts and responses. We can also offer a no-training commitment for production traffic scoped at the account level; that commitment can be captured as an amendment to the DPA.

• Subprocessors & cross-border: we maintain a timestamped subprocessor inventory and a dataflow diagram. The KV cache is ephemeral on GPUs and we do not persist raw request logs to long-term storage unless you enable enhanced telemetry. Some operational telemetry is aggregated and stored in our EU region; any exportable model artifacts (e.g., model snapshots) are under our control plane and are not created from customer data unless a customer explicitly requests model fine-tuning.

We are preparing: 1) dataflow diagram (see draft attached), 2) current subprocessor inventory (spreadsheet attached), and 3) a short "no-training" amendment template that you can use for procurement. Please see attachments. Naomi will follow up with suggested DPA language for the outputs/derivatives paragraph.

Next steps: can you confirm which legal entity will sign and whether Medisoft needs a restricted list of countries for subprocessors?

— Jonas
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

[Attachments: dataflow-diagram-v2.png, redwood-subprocessor-inventory.xlsx, no-train-template-amendment.docx]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@medisoft.io>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david@redwood.ai>, Medisoft Legal <legal@medisoft.io>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on ownership & transfers in DPA — Medisoft

Hi Elena,

Following up with suggested language and a couple of clarifying notes. Below is a candidate clause you can use in the DPA; happy to iterate on wording to match your counsel's style.

Proposed clause (outputs & model improvement):
"Customer Data" means prompts, files, and any content submitted by Customer to the Redwood API.
"Service Outputs" means content generated by models in response to Customer Data.
Redwood acknowledges and agrees that Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in Customer Data and Service Outputs. Redwood will not use Customer Data or Service Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve any model or model weights used in the Redwood service without Customer's prior, written opt-in consent ("No-Training Commitment").

Notes:
• The No-Training Commitment can be applied at the account or legal-entity level and can be time-boxed (e.g., during the initial term or while a subscription is active).
• Operational telemetry (anonymized usage metrics, aggregate token counts) may be retained for service reliability and capacity planning; we can provide a description of telemetry fields and retention periods for Medisoft's review.
• For increased assurance we can: (a) list EU-only subprocessors; (b) provide SOC 2 + ISO27001 certificates; and (c) include an exportability appendix that documents what artifacts, if any, could be exported and under what authorization.

We attached a redline to your draft DPA with this clause and the exportability appendix as a starting point. If Medisoft wants a legally-signed No-Training Commitment we can prepare an amendment for signature and include a short attestation statement for procurement.

Thanks — happy to sync on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Privacy Lead | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: dpa-no-train-proposal-redline.pdf]

From: Elena Rossi <elena@medisoft.io>

Cc: Medisoft Legal <legal@medisoft.io>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on ownership & transfers in DPA — Medisoft

Hi Naomi, Jonas — thanks, this is helpful and faster than expected. A couple of follow-ups from legal/procurement: 

1) Can you provide a signed No-Training Commitment template (PDF) with an attestation date? Procurement needs that to authorize data flows into the sandbox and for the development environment.
2) For subprocessors: procurement wants a list filtered to those with access to telemetry or logs. Can you mark those in the spreadsheet and indicate countries where access occurs?
3) Lastly, we need to confirm exportability for customer-initiated data exports (patient records + generated summaries) — specifically whether exports can be produced in an encrypted archive and whether Redwood will facilitate EU-only egress for exported files.

If you can provide the signed doc and an updated subprocessor sheet by EOD Friday we can move to countersign. If needed we can do a 20-minute call on Thursday to finish outstanding wording.

Thanks — Elena
Head of Integrations, Medisoft
